text:
sam: heads up, got an unusual packing spiral in us-east1 this morning — dozens of 0.25 GPU pods ended up concentrating on rack-4 after a spot reclaim wave, then kubelet eviction churned. anyone else seeing a tiny-pod cluster pattern?
leila: saw it on infra-dashboard, scheduler scheduling_rate dipped and pod_bind_attempts jumped. looks like a sequence: reclaim -> nodes cordon -> offers reorder -> same few nodes win repeatedly.
ryan: which scheduler tuning was live in us-east1? we shipped pack_factor 1.6 last week to reduce idle GPU hours. could be the culprit.
sam: shipped 1.6 yes. sample pod list below:
```
NAME      STATUS   NODE    GPU_REQ
ml-small  Running  rack-4  0.25
ml-tiny   Running  rack-4  0.25
ml-burst  Pending  <none>  0.25
ml-x      Running  rack-4  0.25
```
(Full dump: s3://redwood-ops/incident/6182023333/pod-dump.txt)
sched-bot: NOTICE: node rack-4 marked Cordoned by cloud-controller at 2025-04-02T07:12:10Z due to spot-reclaim.
leila: the pack heuristic multiplies fit_score by pack_factor, so tiny requests get tightly coalesced. During offer reordering the same nodes looked "best" and got a flood. Once kubelet memory pressure hit, evictions requeued and the loop continued.
dana: short fixes: 1) revert pack_factor to 1.0 in us-east1 (quick rollback) 2) for pods <0.5 GPU, enforce a PodTopologySpreadPolicy across racks 3) add a 2-minute jitter to warm-pool handoff to avoid synchronized placement.
ryan: longer: add a circuit-breaker on pack_factor that drops it to 1.0 for 15m following any node cordon in a zone. also expose a metric micro_pod_cluster_ratio for Canary alerts.
sam: ops runbook stepwise: a) rollback pack_factor (dana) b) trigger a controlled rebalance job that evicts and respects spread for small pods (sam) c) add Canary eval for micro clustering (leila).
sched-bot: ACTION created: INC-1459 "us-east1 microgpu spiral" assigned to sam, due 2025-04-02T09:00:00Z.
leila: quick check: losing pack_factor saves ~6% GPU hours but increases cross-rack network egress and slightly higher tail latencies for large-gang jobs. we should add a cost/availability section to the post-incident note.
dana: agreed — will draft tradeoffs. also adding a throttle on immediate warm-pool fulfillment during zone disturbances as a safety net.
ryan: I'll start a canary test for the circuit-breaker in staging, then we can try a controlled failover sim to validate.
sam: thanks — rolling back now, will post when rebalance job completes. :thumbsup:
